svg.title: Controls Plane architecture and operating model
svg.desc: Infographic showing the sidecar request path, decision flow, OpenAPI-to-bundle configuration pipeline, security and failure modes, and repository ownership.
svg.text: Data-level entitlements, masking and data quality for Spring Boot services — no application code changes.
Every request crosses the sidecar. The service only sees traffic that has passed entitlement and DQ.
Deny-first, route-bound, fail-closed. The payload never chooses its own policy.
OpenAPI annotations derive the registry; delivery policy and DQ are merged, validated and signed. OPA Rego stays external.
owned by controls-rules, not the service
OPA Rego: external, not in bundle
Ed25519 signature · digest recomputed by sidecar
render → openapi-diff → controls-check → conformance → sign → publish bundle@digest
* required in production · OPA_URL / PIP TLS optional · OPA Rego stays external
The default posture is deny; every control has an explicit failure path.
read-only replicas; cache and known lag.
Full/partial per field; locked fields always full; error
bundle → no readiness; missing mask policy → no
Hashed identifiers, never payloads. Denials always,
allows sampled; drop/write metrics on the async sink.
Ed25519 manifest.sig; digest recomputed on load and
Three owners, one contract boundary. Policy authority stays central; the service keeps its code.
Legend: solid = request/control path · dashed = response · badges = fail-closed outcome
